description:
FOUND s504 (Fable, 2026-10-02) attributing the full companion run`s movers (#2389).  re/reg_pmod.t moved 58/30 -> 4/24 at 577a09a4 (s496a merged): sig `aborted-forms:1: Character `p` may not follow `(?` in regex; marked by <-- HERE in m/(? <-- HERE p)N/`.  Before #2372 the bad pattern warned and returned no-match, so the loop went on and 58 rows passed (some honestly: the `/p` FLAG spelling works); now the first inline `(?p)` aborts the whole top-level form and 54 rows are never produced (shortfall 0 -> 60).

REPRODUCER ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s504/review/pm1.pl (perl vs main b7ec0093; outputs pm1.perl / pm1.pcl): `"aNb" =~ /(?p)N/`, `/(?^p:N)/`, `/(?pi)n/` -- perl matches all three; PCL dies at each.  `/N/p` with ${^PREMATCH} / ${^MATCH} / ${^POSTMATCH}: see the outputs.

FIX SHAPE: where the regex translator rewrites inline flag groups for cl-ppcre, DROP the `p` flag (perl: since 5.20 the match variables are always available, /p changes nothing) -- one place, the same pass that already handles the flags cl-ppcre lacks.  Probe: `(?p)`, `(?^p)`, `(?p:...)`, `(?ip-x:...)`, `(?-p)` (perl rejects a NEGATED p: "Regexp modifier \"p\" may not appear after the \"-\"" -- keep that a compile error), and ${^PREMATCH} & co. after each.

BAR: pm1.pl == perl; re/reg_pmod.t back to at least 58/30; guard rows in an existing regex Pl/t file.

BOOKKEEPING s504: re/reg_pmod.t`s snapshot row and row-level baselines ARE spliced to 4/24 with this task as the cause of the 54 new rows (the die itself is the ruled #2372 behaviour; what is missing is the flag).

ALSO (same probe, row 4 -- a second, SILENT wrong): after `"aNb" =~ /N/p`, perl reads ${^PREMATCH}=a ${^MATCH}=N ${^POSTMATCH}=b; PCL reads all three EMPTY.  Probe whether they are empty without /p too (perl 5.20+ sets them always) and fix in the same batch if it is the same mechanism; else file it.
subject: An INLINE `p` regex flag -- `(?p)`, `(?^p:...)`, `(?pi)` -- is rejected by the regex compiler ("Character `p` may not follow `(?`"); perl accepts it (and /p is a no-op since 5.20).  Since s496a (#2372, a regex compile error dies) the form aborts: re/reg_pmod.t 58/30 -> 4/24
